title: Bounded-below site comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, with left module sheaves and the coefficient categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The inverse image of the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is fully faithful on the bounded-below derived categories:
$$
\nu_T^*:\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda).
$$
More precisely, the unit of its adjunction with the bounded-below right derived direct image is a natural isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*.
$$
No constructibility or finiteness of the individual module sheaves is assumed.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, with the small sites and coefficient sheaves specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. They are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $L=\nu_T^*$ and $R=\nu_{T,*}$ for the additive module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. A right adjoint preserves kernels (their universal property is transported by the Hom adjunction), so $R$ is left exact. The finite-level proposition gives exactness of $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], termwise $L$ induces a functor on $D^+$ and preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
For $K\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ choose a representing complex $C$ and $a$ with $H^n(C)=0$ for $n<a$. Its good truncation $M=\tau_{\ge a}C$, zero below $a$, with $M^a=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{a-1})$ and $M^n=C^n$ above $a$, has the same cohomology as $C$ in all degrees: in degree $a$ the kernel of the induced differential is $\ker d_C^a/\operatorname{im}d_C^{a-1}$, and the images and kernels in the higher degrees are unchanged. Thus $C\to M$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] on the small ringed etale site to obtain $M\to I$, with $I$ bounded below and termwise injective. It represents $K$, and $LI$ represents $LK$. The same resolution lemma applies on the pro-etale site.

source.place: 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), second paragraph; good truncation as in Derived Categories 013J, and ringed-site injective resolutions 07A5 with Derived Categories 013K

proof.text:
The two module categories have enough injectives, as can also be recovered from the bounded-below resolution statement without a commutativity restriction. Resolve $F[0]\to J$. Starting at the lowest nonzero degree below zero, exactness there makes the differential injective; the injection of this injective term splits. Remove the resulting two-term contractible direct summand and repeat up to degree $-1$. This is a finite induction because $J$ is bounded below. The remaining degree-zero term is a direct summand of $J^0$, hence injective, and $H^0(J)=F$ is its kernel of the outgoing differential, so embeds in that injective term. Direct summands are injective because a map into a summand can be extended into the injective object and projected back.
Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] defines $\mathbf R R:D^+(\mathcal B)\to D^+(\mathcal A)$ with a natural comparison $\alpha_N:Q(RN)\to\mathbf R R(QN)$, invertible on bounded-below injective complexes. Here $Q$ denotes the appropriate localization. The notation $R\nu_{T,*}$ in the statement means this right derived functor.

source.place: 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic); existence on the ringed sites as in 07A5

proof.text:
We construct the derived adjunction and identify its unit, rather than assuming an adjunction for a scheme morphism. For a bounded-below complex $M$ of $\mathcal A$ and a bounded-below complex $N$ of $\mathcal B$, resolve $N\to J$ by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. This lemma also says $J$ is K-injective; [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to $L\dashv R$ in the convention that $R$ is the right adjoint and $L$ is exact, and makes $RJ$ K-injective. The injective calculation of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies $\mathbf R R(QN)$ with $Q(RJ)$. The Hom-localization bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the homotopy adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(Q(LM),QN)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(LM,J)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M,RJ)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QM,\mathbf R R(QN)).
$$
All complexes here are bounded below, so these are also the Hom sets in $D^+$. Each bijection is natural; maps between injective representatives are represented uniquely up to homotopy by the same Hom-localization bijection, so changing the resolution does not change the bijection. This gives $L\dashv\mathbf R R$. If $j:LM\to J$ is a resolution, the identity of $Q(LM)$ is represented by $j$, whose transpose is $Rj\circ\eta_M$. Thus its unit at $QM$ is represented by $M\xrightarrow{\eta_M}RLM\xrightarrow{Rj}RJ$, or equivalently $Q(\eta_M)$ followed by $\alpha_{LM}$, under the localization identifications.

source.place: 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); explicit Hom calculation following their proofs

proof.text: Use the injective representative $I$ of $K$ chosen in step 1. The finite-level proposition states $R^qR(LI^n)=0$ for every $q>0$ and every $n$. Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $j:LI\to J$ on the pro-etale site. Each $J^n$ is $R$-acyclic by clause 1 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]; its hypotheses of abelian categories with enough injectives hold by steps 1 and 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso] to $j$ and the left exact additive functor $R$: $LI$ and $J$ are bounded below (use the smaller of their lower bounds), every term of both is $R$-acyclic, and $j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $Rj:RLI\to RJ$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By the natural comparison $\alpha$, and its invertibility at $J$, this identifies $Q(RLI)$ with $\mathbf R R(LK)$, with comparison exactly $Q(Rj)$ followed by $\alpha_J$ and the inverse transport along $\mathbf R R(Qj)$. This is the bounded-below acyclic-resolution calculation in the blueprint; a Cartan--Eilenberg spectral sequence is unnecessary once this existing lemma is cited.

source.place: 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), applied as in Pro-etale Cohomology 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), second paragraph

proof.text: The finite-level proposition makes $\eta_{I^n}:I^n\to RLI^n$ an isomorphism for every $n$. The termwise adjunction lemma says these components form a chain map $\eta_I$, since naturality gives $RL(d_I^n)\eta_{I^n}=\eta_{I^{n+1}}d_I^n$. Multiplying this equation by the inverses shows that the inverse components also form a chain map. Thus $\eta_I:I\to RLI$ is an isomorphism of complexes. Step 3 identifies the derived unit at $QI$ with $Q(Rj\circ\eta_I)$; step 4 makes $Q(Rj)$ invertible, and the termwise unit is invertible as just checked. Hence the derived unit is invertible at $QI$, and therefore at $K$ by its naturality and the isomorphism $K\cong QI$. The unit is natural from step 3, so its pointwise inverses form the claimed natural isomorphism.

source.place: 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), final paragraph of the proof, with the derived unit identified in step 3

proof.text:
For $K,H\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, step 3 gives the adjunction bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\mathcal B)}(LK,LH)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\mathcal A)}(K,\mathbf R R(LH)).
$$
By step 5, composition with the unit $\eta_H^D:H\to\mathbf R R(LH)$ gives a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(K,H)$ to the Hom set on the right. The adjunction sends $L(f)$ to $\mathbf R R(Lf)\eta_K^D=\eta_H^D f$ by naturality. Thus the actual map on Hom sets induced by $L$ is the composite of two bijections, proving full faithfulness. Both functors take values in $D^+$ by steps 1 and 2; no boundedness above or constructibility was used.
